themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis Erupts
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 12 THIS WEEK—a 1271% surge versus 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.25)—suggesting a sudden, acute disturbance pattern affecting recreational spaces in Jackson Heights/Elmhurst/Corona.
evidence: 12 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (1271% increase)
z-score of 14.25 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Signal emerged abruptly in past 7 days with no prior escalation
reporting_angles: Visit parks during peak hours to document noise source (concerts, sports events, gatherings, mechanical issues)
Interview Parks Department and residents about what triggered sudden surge and whether enforcement response is underway

themes_detail.label: Green Taxi Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Green taxi complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK versus 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 5.67), signaling a concentrated service or conduct problem affecting residents in the district.
evidence: 4 green taxi complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase)
z-score of 5.67 confirms statistically significant spike
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details to identify specific taxi medallions, drivers, or violations (refusal of service, unsafe driving, fare disputes)
Contact TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) to determine if enforcement action is planned and interview affected riders

themes_detail.label: Tree Deaths Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK versus 1.2 weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 5.67), pointing to a sudden environmental decline or disease outbreak in the district's street canopy.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (300% increase)
Community Board budget records show repeated 'park maintenance and safety requests' to Parks Department over multiple years, indicating unmet need
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations and investigate potential cause (disease, storm damage, street salt exposure, neglect)
Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance budgets and canopy health; cross-reference with long-standing CB budget requests for park upkeep

themes_detail.label: Park Disorder and Loitering Spike
themes_detail.summary: Violation of park rules jumped to 4 complaints LAST WEEK (1500% increase versus 0.2 weekly average), coinciding with the park noise crisis and elevated homeless assistance requests (9 complaints 3 weeks ago, 279% spike), suggesting coordinated enforcement gaps or emerging encampments.
evidence: 4 park rules violations LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score: 5.67)
9 homeless person assistance calls 3 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average (279% increase, z-score: 4.43)
Drinking complaints LAST WEEK: 6 vs. 1.2 weekly average (380% increase)
Convergence of three related safety issues suggests systemic park management failure
reporting_angles: Investigate whether Parks Enforcement Patrol (PEP) staffing is adequate; request precinct data on park-related arrests and quality-of-life enforcement
Interview homeless services providers and shelter operators about capacity and outreach in Jackson Heights parks; identify which parks are affected

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Infrastructure Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 8 LAST WEEK versus 0.6 weekly average (1180% increase, z-score: 7.43), indicating residents perceive inadequate trash receptacles; combined with chronic 'street lights' and 'park maintenance' budget requests, suggests deferred infrastructure investment.
evidence: 8 litter basket requests LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (1180% increase, z-score: 7.43)
Community Board budget records show repeated 'repair street lights' and 'park maintenance' requests year-over-year
Pattern suggests systemic underfunding of streetscape infrastructure
reporting_angles: Request DSNY data on litter basket inventory, maintenance schedules, and planned installations in CD 403
Interview CB members about why infrastructure requests are recurring year after year; identify which streets/parks lack adequate receptacles
